Volume record (feed volumes/LOEtAAAAMAAJ): Afro-Pub, 1980, 680 pages, viewability no_pages; identifier UOM:39015049415675; HathiTrust bib API record 000127644 'Co…
new_statements.relation_note: States that Jiru has three level tones; also treats denasalization of final consonants in Jiru. Full text is print-only (no scan online; HathiTrust/Google full view unavailable); statement seen in Google's snippet text only.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Jiru is a tone language with three level tones (like Shimizu's Proto-Jukunoid, Yukuben, Kpan, Jukun and Chomo; contrast Kutep and Icen with four); nothing about stress/accent is visible in the snippets.
new_statements.exceptions: none visible in the snippet; a nearby snippet mentions tonal restrictions by word class ('.. tone never occurs with a noun stem and top tone never occurs with a verb') whose subject language cannot be determined from the snippet
new_statements.identity_note: Shimizu's 'Jiru' is his own field data from Gindin Dorawa (snippet: 'Apart from Gindin Dorawa, where I collected my data of Jiru, the only other known place which seems to be a Jiru settlement is Zhiru on the southern bank of the Benue. Maybe there are some Jiru at Wurbo on the R. Donga'); this is the work Glottolog uses as Glottolog's most extensive description for jiru1238 and the Jiru [jrr] of Ethnologue (Zhiru, Wurbo cluster, Karim Lamido LGA). Not Jibu [jib] or Jiba [juo].

Any tone-marked Jiru forms or a per-language phonological note would be here; Jukunoid languages are tonal, so at best this would yield a tone statement, not a stress rule.

sources.note: Nothing phonological about any Wurbo lect; Table 1 (p. 6) lists 'Jukunoid / North / Hone, Kiyu' among the area's languages; section 3.3.2 gives migration traditions only. The words 'stress'/'stressful' occur only in the ecological sense (pp. 7, 30).
